r.정치 구도: In 2011 a popular uprising and NATO air strikes brought down a dictatorship that had lasted more than 40 years. The governments set up afterward never took hold, and from 2014 the country split between east and west. In the west, Tripoli is home to a unity government recognized by the UN, while in the east a parliament and an armed force called the Libyan National Army control territory reaching into the south. After a 2020 ceasefire a presidential election was set for December 2021, but disputes over candidates and election laws scrapped it, and no national election has been held since. In August 2026 the two sides agreed through UN mediation to hold elections within 24 months, but similar promises have been broken many times, so hopes are low. Militias also clash often inside Tripoli, and in May 2025 heavy fighting broke out in the city center.

t.why: Libya has the largest oil reserves in Africa and faces Europe across the Mediterranean. Control of oil revenue is at the heart of the split, so when one side blockades oil fields and export terminals, output can drop sharply overnight. In 2024 the two sides clashed over who would run the central bank, and the east shut down oil production. Turkey backs the western government, while Russia, the United Arab Emirates and Egypt back the eastern camp, turning the country into an arena for foreign powers. Migrants who cross the Sahara set off from here for Italy, so Libya is tied directly to European migration policy. In September 2023 a storm burst two dams and killed thousands in the eastern city of Derna.
t.rel: Since the regime fell in 2011, it has been split between rival governments in the east and west. Foreign powers such as Turkey, Russia and the UAE back each side, and it is a departure point for migrants to Europe.
t.korea: Diplomatic relations began in December 1980, and Korea opened an embassy in Tripoli the following year. Korean construction companies poured in after that. Dong Ah Construction took on the first phase of the Great Man-Made River project in the 1980s, piping groundwater from under the desert to coastal cities, and it became a symbol of Korea's Middle East construction boom. By the Korean foreign ministry's count, Korean companies have won about $36.8 billion in construction contracts in Libya. Most Korean residents and workers left during the 2011 civil war, and the Korean government now bans travel to the whole country. Even so, in September 2026 the two governments held an economic cooperation forum in Tripoli to help Korean firms win construction work.
t.know: Libya has the largest proven oil reserves in Africa.
etext: Libya has Africa's largest proven oil reserves, and its high-quality crude sits close to European buyers. In June 2026 daily output recovered to its highest level since 2013. An undersea pipeline also carries gas to Italy.

The National Oil Corporation sells the oil, and the central bank in Tripoli collects and distributes the money. The eastern and western governments fight for a bigger share, so oil field blockades and rival budgets keep coming back.

Beyond oil there is almost no industry to speak of. Most of the budget goes to public sector wages and fuel subsidies, and the sovereign wealth fund's assets have been frozen under UN sanctions since 2011. Banks often run short of cash, forcing people to queue, and the black market exchange rate drifts away from the official one.
